images.caption:
Former Unitarian Chapel Nottingham:
The chapel was opened in 1876, built to a design of the architect Stuart Colman, of Bristol. It was used as a place of worship for Unitarian Presbyterians in Nottingham until 1982. It was then converted into the Nottingham Lace Museum, but this venture proved financially unviable. The building was then converted to its current use, as a Pitcher and Piano public house.

images.filename: UK Newark on Trent cemetery polish Presidents.jpg
images.caption: Graves of Polish President-in-Exile in front of the Polish war memorial in the Commonwealth War Cemetery, Newark-on-Trent, England. The headstone of Stanisław Ostrowski is nearest the camera. Next is the headstone of August Zaleski, and behind it the headstone of Władysław Raczkiewicz. Nearest the war memorial is the ledger stone where Władysław Sikorski was buried until his remains were translated to Warsaw in 1993.
images.alt: Graves of Polish President-in-Exile in front of the Polish war memorial in the Commonwealth War Cemetery, Newark-on-Trent, England. The headstone of Stanisław Ostrowski is nearest the camera. Next is the headstone of August Zaleski, and behind it the headstone of Władysław Raczkiewicz. Nearest the war memorial is the ledger stone where Władysław Sikorski was buried until his remains were translated to Warsaw in 1993.

images.caption: The Jewry Wall and St Nicholas' Church in Leicester, England. The wall is the second largest piece of surviving civil Roman building in Britain, and is both a Scheduled Monument and a Grade I listed building. Originally it separated the Palaestra from the Frigidarium at Ratae Corieltauvorum's baths. St Nicholas' Church is also Grade I listed, and dates from AD 880.
